paper.title_en: Padé-screened quantum-corrected black holes: Ringdown spectroscopy and extreme-mass-ratio dephasing as complementary gravitational-wave probes
paper.abstract_en: It remains unclear which gravitational-wave channel constrains which feature of a black-hole deformation. We address this for a new two-parameter family of static black holes in which the leading inverse-cube quantum correction to the Newtonian potential is resummed by a Padé approximant into a bounded mass function, <math altimg="si106.svg"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak">−</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><msup><mi>ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo linebreak="goodbreak">/</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo linebreak="badbreak">+</mo><msup><mi>ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></math>. The screening amplitude ϵ and length ℓ fix a cubic horizon equation, an effective source obeying the null and weak energy conditions for ϵ > 0, and a strictly positive axial perturbation potential. We compute the <math altimg="si4.svg"><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> and <math altimg="si107.svg"><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> quasinormal modes with a Chebyshev spectral solver, validated against Schwarzschild and time-domain evolutions, and evolve adiabatic extreme-mass-ratio inspirals with exact geodesic energetics. A Bayesian analysis of explicitly synthetic ringdown data shows that a third-generation event bounds the tail coefficient <math altimg="si108.svg"><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>ℓ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> to |κ| < 0.11 at 90% credibility and detects a benchmark deviation with <math altimg="si109.svg"><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mi mathvariant="script">B</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>6.86</mn></mrow></math>. A year-long inspiral into a 10<sup loc="post">6</sup> M⊙ black hole accumulates a dephasing |ΔΦ| ≈ 7.71 × 10<sup loc="post">4</sup> |κ| rad ( ≈ 20% flux-model uncertainty), giving sensitivity to <math altimg="si110.svg"><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>∼</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> when ℓ scales with mass; for fixed ℓ, stellar-mass ringdowns give the stronger bound. Because both channels depend predominantly on κ, combining them breaks the ϵ–ℓ degeneracy only weakly.
